claude.country: Multinational (four public datasets across five countries, including Argentina, Brazil, United States)

links.outcome: Malignancy model performance after filtering out-of-distribution images by SAGE score threshold
links.effect: Filtering images by SAGE score thresholds improved performance of a separate malignancy prediction model; approach robust to image modality changes and new diagnostic classes (no numbers in abstract).
links.quote: We show how filtering images based on SAGE score thresholds can improve the performance of a separate malignancy prediction model

openai.country: Five countries, including Argentina, Brazil, and the United States

links.effect: SAGE quantified likeness of images from Argentina, Brazil and the United States to HAM10000 and identified problematic artifacts affecting reliability.
links.quote: Using our method, Supervised Autoencoders for Generalization Estimates (SAGE), we quantify likeness of images from patients in Argentina, Brazil and the United States to the popular HAM10000 benchmarking dataset and identify problematic image artifacts that affect the reliability of predictions in a pre-clinical setting.

links.outcome: OOD filtering and malignancy prediction performance
links.effect: SAGE detected OOD images from four datasets across five countries; threshold filtering improved separate model performance, with no numeric gain reported.
links.quote: We show how filtering images based on SAGE score thresholds can improve the performance of a separate malignancy prediction model and how our approach is robust to variations in image modality and the introduction of new diagnostic classes, providing users with a powerful tool for interrogating key differences between their data and the training distribution of an ML model before clinical implementation.
